subject: [PATCH 05/46] mm/truncate: look again if a folio left the mapping

reviews.author: David (Arm)
reviews.summary: Reviewer noted that the 'index >= end' condition might prevent another lookup needed for concurrent truncation of a large folio, and requested clarification on whether this is intended behavior.
reviews.raw_body:
For truncate_inode_pages_range() I *think* the "index >= end" might prevent
another lookup that we would need.

Assume we have a large folio with 512 pages for simplicity, and we want to
punch-hole the first half of it.

The whole partial splitting logic (truncate_inode_partial_folio) will first
split that folio buddy-like into various folios.

Now we want to remove the split folios in the loop:

index = 0;
end = 256;
while (index < 256)
	if (!find_get_entries(mapping, &index, 255, &fbatch, ...

	-> Returns our split folios from the buddy split, the last one should
           cover pages 128 to 255
	-> Sets index = 256

Then we have the concurrent stuff happening. We wouldn't re-execute the
find_get_entries() even though a folio was replaced in the meantime, as index =256.

My brain hurts, does the above make sense?

-- 
Cheers,

David

2026-10-28.patch_summary: This patch addresses a potential race condition in the folio locking mechanism when truncating a file. The issue arises from the fact that the reference count check is performed before acquiring the folio lock, which can lead to unexpected behavior if another CPU has already unlocked the folio. To fix this, the patch ensures that the folio lock is acquired after the reference count check, preventing the race condition and ensuring correct truncation of files.
